column1: # THE COMPONENT PROP SURFACE, as data.
# One row per prop per component: what a component reads, what type it
# takes, whether it is required, and what it does. A machine-readable
# restatement of reference-components.md, published so that a generator
# driving Jostraca from another language can pin its own schema against
# this file rather than against a page of prose.
# It is published for reading, not for importing. There is no package
# edge: fetch this file at a tag, vendor it, and pin it -- Jostraca takes
# no dependency on its consumers and its consumers take none on it. The
# version it describes is the tag it was fetched at; nothing is stamped
# in the file, because a stamp is one more thing that can go stale.
# WHAT KEEPS IT TRUE: ts/test/cmp-surface.test.ts reads this file and
# the components beside it, and fails when the two disagree -- a prop
# read by a component with no row here, a row naming a prop no component
# reads, or a component whose refusal of an unknown prop does not match
# what its `*` row claims. go/cmp_surface_test.go holds the Go port to
# the same `*` rows through the data path, which is where the two ports
# have to agree because it is the surface a data tree reaches.
# FORMAT: tab-separated, one case per line, with a header row. Lines
# that are blank or start with `#` are ignored. This is the same shape
# as the shared corpus in test/spec, and deliberately NOT in that
# directory: both stacks' spec runners read every .tsv there as function
# cases and fail on an unknown `fn`.
#   cmp       the component, spelled as it is exported and as a tree's
#   prop      the prop; `*` is the row for every prop NOT listed
#   type      string, number, boolean, object, array, any, or a `|`
#             union. A data tree carries JSON, so a RegExp or a function
#             is reachable only from a generator written in the host
#   note      what it does. A note beginning `unused:` marks a prop both
#             ports accept and neither reads; `refused:` and `ignored:`
#             on a `*` row say what an unknown prop does
# NOT LISTED, deliberately: `ctx$`. It is the ambient context, written
# into every props object by `cmp()` and never by an author. Every
# component receives it and no tree should ever state it.
# ALSO NOT LISTED: the props a PARENT binds for one invocation of its
# `{item.path}` means something, and a child receives them whether or
# not its own row set names them. They are bindings rather than props an
